players.product: busways, PDUs and rack power distribution

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026: strong sales growth of +18.3% excluding currency effects, comprising organic growth of +9.3% and +8.2% growth through acquisitions; adjusted operating margin very strong and resilient at 20.7% despite input inflation; net profit EUR 335 million (+14% YoY); free cash flow EUR 221 million (8.7% of sales). By geography (like-for-like): North and Central America +25.8% driven by data-center offerings in the US; Europe -2.8% in a contrasted building market; rest of world -1.8% despite very nice growth in India. Sales up +9% like-for-like while headcount slightly decreasing — strong SG&A leverage.
quarterly_data.figure: Sales +18.3% ex-FX (organic +9.3%, acquisitions +8.2%); adjusted operating margin 20.7%; net profit EUR 335 million (+14%); FCF EUR 221 million (8.7% of sales); North/Central America +25.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center offerings grew around +30% like-for-like in Q1 (slightly above +30% in the US, the hottest market), after +40% in 2025 and +15% in 2024. Data center was 26% of group sales last year and should be around 30% this year (could reach 35% or 40% over time without concern). Growth attributed to hyperscalers massively increasing their investments — a wave expected to last for years; NO pre-buy seen. Fastest-growing product families: COOLING (aisle door containment), the whole powertrain, and Avtron load banks ('fantastic growth'); global coverage from medium voltage down to compute architecture and cooling. Recent data-center acquisitions: Avtron, Kratos Industries (MV/LV switchgear, US), Linkk Busway Systems (Malaysia).
quarterly_data.figure: Data center ~+30% like-for-like in Q1 (US slightly above +30%); 26% of sales last year moving to ~30%; grew +40% in 2025, +15% in 2024

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 targets confirmed: sales growth excluding currency of +10% to +15%, comprising organic growth of +4% to +7% and +6% to +8% from acquisitions; adjusted operating margin after acquisitions of 20.5% to 21% of sales. Data-center growth expectation revised to the HIGHER END of the 10%-20% range given Q1 and the large number of orders. Global guidance not raised despite the DC strength because of added geopolitical uncertainty on the building side; pricing plan lifted to +2%-+3% (from +1%-+2%) to offset purchase-price inflation now seen around +4%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026: sales +10% to +15% ex-FX (organic +4% to +7%, acquisitions +6% to +8%); margin 20.5% to 21%; data center toward high end of 10%-20%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and cost dynamics: Legrand has scaled with US data-center demand WITHOUT materially changing its CapEx-to-sales ratio of about 2% — 'data center is not a CapEx-intensive industry' for Legrand — absorbing ramp inefficiencies (air freight, subcontracting, overtime) without significant P&L impact. Gross margin down 190 basis points as pricing of +2.3% did not yet compensate inflation of +4.2% on raw materials/components and +3% on personnel cost (half of the ~4% purchase-price increase is tariff effect); gap expected to ease through the year. Four acquisitions announced so far in 2026, all in data centers and energy transition, representing combined annual revenue of around EUR 275 million.
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx ~2% of sales maintained; pricing +2.3% vs raw-material inflation +4.2%; four 2026 acquisitions ~EUR 275 million combined revenue

quarterly_data.signal: 800V DC architecture stance unchanged: 'We believe it's gonna come. We believe that it's gonna be more progressive than some of you expect' — Legrand sees itself well-positioned for both hybrid architectures and full DC, viewing the shift as an opportunity (more data centers, higher density, more energy efficient) rather than a threat. More detail promised at the capital markets day in Singapore on September 29, 2026, with a particular focus on data centers. In UPS, Legrand is a small player (industrial and increasingly data-center use); not a significant inverter player.
